title: Choose a direction for Wordvale
question: Which direction feels right for the full app?

options.label: Reading Room
options.thesis: A calm, warm workspace that makes the recording and its transcript the center of attention.
options.viewport: A familiar sidebar and toolbar frame a generous recording workspace; queue and transcript become the focus.
options.risk: Warmth must not compromise contrast or dense-work efficiency.

raised.raise: Clear hierarchy separates active work from navigation.
Dense lists remain easy to scan.
A consistent alignment system carries every screen.
Secondary details reveal themselves in place.
Recording durations and order remain legible.
Status is readable without relying on color.

options.label: Studio Desk
options.thesis: A restrained native-feeling workspace with a focused transcript canvas and a compact inspector.
options.viewport: A compact sidebar and top toolbar put import, queue and transcript review in one clear workspace.
options.risk: Its familiar Mac-app grammar can feel conventional.

options.label: Metro
options.thesis: A source of discipline for the workspace.
options.viewport: Familiar Mac controls retain their expected behavior.
options.case: Its literal presentation is less clear and less familiar for everyday transcription.
options.risk: A literal adaptation could obscure the workflow.
